requirements.evidence: Migration has the FK cascade, nullable invited_by, role default, unique (entity_id,email) (create_entity_invites_table.php:16-24). The model mutator lowercases and trims e-mails (EntityInvite.php:41-46). Members::sendInvite authorizes, validates, rejects existing members and pending invites, replaces expired ones, turns a UniqueConstraintViolationException into an inviteEmail error, rate-limits only successful invites (RateLimiter::hit after creation), queues the mail, writes an audit log and resets the form (Members.php:57-131). PendingInvites accept/decline: 403 for non-invitees, expired -> 'invite' error, idempotent, firstOrCreate, session + redirect (PendingInvites.php:19-73). Modal title is ui.members_details, the select has no empty option, confirmRemoval modal uses ui.members_remove_title. Mail strings and pt_BR translations are present. Onboarding <hr> appears only when invites exist (pending-invites.blade.php:2-3).

conventions.evidence: Livewire uses #[Validate] + $this->validate() (Members.php:27-31). The factory and migration have down(). Docs (business-rules.md, database-schema.md) and CHANGELOG are updated. However, the new domain writes (create invite, accept invite -> create membership, cancel/decline) live inline in the components instead of app/Actions/*. Invitee authorization is a hand-rolled abort_unless in PendingInvites::inviteFor (PendingInvites.php:93-98) rather than a policy. The CHANGELOG entry is also duplicated into the released [0.0.0] section.

security.evidence: Every mutating action authorizes server-side: sendInvite/cancelInvite use authorize('update', $this->entity); saveRole resolves the membership through $this->entity->memberships() and authorizes assignRole; removeMember keeps its owner and last-manager guards. Action IDs are re-resolved and scoped (cancelInvite uses $this->entity->invites()->findOrFail). A tamper test covers selectedMembershipId. All output uses {{ }}. $fillable is declared via #[Fillable]. Minor gap: invitee authorization bypasses the policy layer, and confirmRemoval/cancelRemoval/closeMember are public without authorize (they only toggle UI state).

tests.evidence: InviteTest.php and MembersTest.php cover: schema/unique index, factory and expired state, lowercase normalization, mail en/pt_BR rendering, case-insensitive listing, accept happy path, a non-invitee accept/decline (unauthorized), expired, idempotent accept, onboarding hr/no-hr, switcher, employee 403 on page/route/actions, invalid email/role including owner, existing member, pending vs expired, unique race, rate limit with free invalid input, single help is-danger, foreign membership open/save tamper, owner immutable, last-manager demotion, removal modal and state reset.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses the existing policies and audit log. managerCount() deduplicates the manager-count query (Members.php:237-242). Small speculative bits: the owner-role fallback in accept ('$invite->role === UserRole::Owner ? UserRole::Employee', PendingInvites.php:38) for a state that validation never allows, the unused inviter() relation, and a double trim in sendInvite (trim before validate, then mb_strtolower(trim()) again, and the mutator trims once more).

readability.evidence: Clear names and focused methods, with short intent comments (e.g. 'Lost a race against a concurrent invite'). The view is well-structured, with an accessible modal (role=dialog, aria-labelledby). sendInvite is long-ish (~75 lines) and would read better as an Action.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. The navbar/dashboard link changes (default-page.blade.php:44-46, dashboard.blade.php:17-21) support the manager-only requirement. The stray duplicate CHANGELOG entry under the released [0.0.0] section (CHANGELOG.md:40) rewrites release history unrelated to the task.

issues.explanation: The new domain writes (send/cancel invite, accept/decline invite creating a membership) are done inline in Livewire components instead of one app/Actions class per use case, as the conventions require.
Invitee authorization is a hand-rolled abort_unless e-mail comparison instead of a policy/gate, contrary to 'authorization always goes through policies'.
The invite entry is also added under the already-released [0.0.0] section, falsifying release history.
Defensive owner->employee fallback covers a state that validation and the migration flow never produce.
The e-mail is trimmed/lowercased three times (property trim, local mb_strtolower(trim()), model mutator).
closeMember/confirmRemoval/cancelRemoval are public without authorize; harmless UI-state toggles, but the project policy says to authorize every public action.

review.summary: The change replaces direct member addition with a complete invite flow (table, model, factory, queued mail, PendingInvites component) and a manager-only members page with a detail modal, explicit saveRole and a confirmation modal. Requirements, edge cases (races, rate limits, idempotency, tamper) and tests are thoroughly covered. Approval with nits/minor changes: domain writes bypass the project's Actions pattern, invitee authorization skips policies, and the CHANGELOG entry is duplicated into a released section.
